items.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013
items.q: playing with Freddie Hubbard for eight years, his approach to running a band I appreciate so much more now than I did when I was in the band

ctx.x: And I’ll tell you why, personally not much. Because I play with a lot of people who played with Art. Art had such a strong personality that a lot of the guys who played with Art took on his personality. Freddie Hubbard, Jackie McLean, Benny Golson, Terrance Blanchard, Donald Harrison — a lot of these guys that I played with. And their philosophical approach to the music and to the bandstand, and that was, first and foremost, highest level of respect for the audience. That’s first and foremost, that you don’t…

know, because, like I said, playing with Freddie Hubbard for eight years, his approach to running a band I appreciate so much more now than I did when I was in the band. Because he was not the kind of bandleader who was very hands-on. Like I think in eight years I was with him we had five rehearsals and three of those were for record dates. Because his mindset was we’ve got a gig, learn the music, and I’m going to call it and you just better know it.
How did you learn the music?
